# Amazon Polly's Generative Voices Get More Expressive, and Hindi and Finnish Are Now Generally Available

> **In short:** Amazon says its Polly Generative voice engine now sounds more expressive and accurate, with low delay, and adds 14 new voices across 9 locales. Hindi and Finnish are now generally available. The upgrade needs no code changes.

Have you ever listened to a computer voice read a long message and felt it was reading to you, not talking with you? That flat, robotic rhythm is exactly what newer voice models aim to fix. Amazon has announced a major upgrade to one of them.

## What Amazon Polly is

Amazon Polly is a text-to-speech service, meaning it turns written words into spoken audio. Companies use it to power things like audio versions of articles, phone systems, navigation prompts, and voice features inside apps. The "Generative" engine is a newer kind of voice model. Instead of stitching together pre-recorded sounds, it generates speech based on patterns it learned from a large amount of human voice data. (A model, in this context, is the trained software that does the work.)

## What Amazon says changed

According to Amazon's announcement, the upgrade brings three main improvements:

- **More expressive speech.** The voice should sound more natural, with better emotion and rhythm.
- **More accurate speech.** The engine should pronounce words the way the text intends.
- **Low latency.** Latency is the short delay between sending text and hearing the first sound. Lower latency means the voice starts talking quickly, which matters for live conversations.

Amazon also says the update is a drop-in upgrade. That means existing setups can move to the new version without rewriting code. It is now generally available in production, which means it is ready for real, live services rather than still in testing.

## New voices and languages

Amazon reports 14 new voices across 9 locales. A locale is a language plus a regional variation, such as the way English is spoken in one country versus another. The company also announced that Hindi and Finnish are now generally available. The announcement does not list every voice name or every locale in the text we have, so check Amazon's official Polly documentation for the full list before planning a project around a specific voice.

## What this means for you

- **For your business or work**: If your company sends voice messages, reads documents aloud, or runs a phone system, a more natural voice may make customers feel better served. Ask your developer or IT team whether your current setup already uses Polly, since Amazon describes the upgrade as requiring no code changes.
- **For accessibility and content**: More expressive speech can make audio versions of written material easier to follow for people who prefer listening, including people with reading difficulties.
- **If you're just getting started**: You don't need to build anything to benefit. Watch for products and apps that mention Polly, and try listening to their voices to hear the difference for yourself.
- **If you already use it**: If you run Polly in production, test a few of your longest or most emotional scripts on the new engine and compare the pacing. Keep an eye on latency in your live features, since Amazon highlights it as a key improvement.

## Wrap-up

Amazon says its Polly Generative engine now offers more natural, more accurate speech with lower delay, plus 14 new voices and generally available Hindi and Finnish. The upgrade is designed to slot in without code changes. Your next step today: open Amazon's official Polly documentation, check which voices and locales your project needs, and listen to a sample before you decide anything.
